evidence.note: Built a dedicated benchmark.py early and ran it across all 10 evaluation shapes, reporting per-shape medians (e.g. shapes 8/9 at 71.9ms/133.6ms) rather than single untimed samples.
Tracked 'median time for Shape 9' and used it to compare TF32 vs baseline — medians drive optimization decisions, not intuition.
Explicitly framed the target as 'the maximum of the 10 per-shape medians' vs the H100 budget and identified Shape 9 (N=2048) as the binding worst-case shape to target.
Wrote grade.py modeled on the grader — checks correctness across 10 shapes and computes median execution times — a reusable grader-faithful instrument.
Re-ran the grader/benchmark after nearly every change (TF32/FP16/BF16/torch.compile), re-checking latency numbers each time rather than assuming.

reasoning: The agent went well beyond ad-hoc timing: it built a benchmark and a grader-replica (grade.py), consistently used per-shape medians across all 10 shapes, evaluated the max, targeted the binding shape (Shape 9), and re-measured after each change — matching much of anchor 8. But the visible trajectory never explicitly confirms the finer grader protocol (warmup discard, per-iteration input regeneration, CUDA-event timing) and shows no accounting for measurement noise or confirmation of margin under budget, which keeps it below a full 8 and well short of 10. This places it at 7, between the median-based discipline of anchor 5 and the fully grader-faithful harness of anchor 8.
